about: The new-app intake (ADR-0058): the question cards the new-app skill shows the owner, and the test tools for each kind of test. New-KitApp checks the answers against this file and writes them to the app's docs/app-profile.md. Each card's first option is its recommendation. A card with dependsOn shows only the options whose fits lists the other card's answer. Every option and tool has a cost label: Free, Free tier (free up to a limit) or Paid, with the price, its source and the date checked.

cards.question: What kind of app is it?

options.label: Web API and a Blazor web app
options.description: An ASP.NET Core API with a Blazor web front end. The API can serve a phone app later. Fits most apps people use in a browser.

options.label: Web API only
options.description: An ASP.NET Core HTTP API with no user interface of its own, for other apps or services to call.

options.label: Blazor web app only
options.description: A Blazor web app with no separate API: the pages read and write the data themselves.

options.label: .NET MAUI app (phone or desktop)
options.description: A native app for Android, iOS, Windows or macOS, built with .NET MAUI.

cards.question: Where does the app keep its data, and what shape is it?

options.label: On a server, as related tables
options.description: Records that refer to each other, such as customers and their orders, shared by every user. Most business apps.

options.label: On a server, as documents
options.description: Items read by one key, with a shape that changes often, or data spread across regions.

options.label: Only on the user's device
options.description: Each user's data stays in the app on their phone or computer; nothing is shared.

options.label: It keeps no data
options.description: The app stores nothing of its own, for example a calculator or a front end to another service.

options.label: Azure SQL Database, free offer
options.description: SQL Server in Azure, free up to a monthly limit, and paused rather than billed past it. Tests run on SQL Server in a container.

options.label: Azure Database for PostgreSQL
options.description: PostgreSQL in Azure: free for 12 months with an Azure free account, then billed.

options.label: Azure Cosmos DB, free tier
options.description: A document database in Azure, free up to 1000 RU/s and 25 GB for the account's life.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: A database in a file inside the app. Free.

cards.question: Who signs in to the app?

options.label: Customers or the public
options.description: People sign in with Microsoft Entra External ID: email, or a Google or Microsoft account. The app never stores passwords (SEC-008).

cost.label: Free tier
cost.free: The first 50,000 monthly active users; add-ons such as SMS codes have no free amount
cost.price: Past 50,000 monthly active users: not verified

options.label: People in one organization
options.description: Staff sign in with their work account in Microsoft Entra ID. The app never stores passwords (SEC-008).

cost.label: Free tier
cost.free: Microsoft Entra ID Free: users, groups and single sign-on
cost.price: P1 and P2, for Conditional Access and ID Protection: not verified

options.label: No sign-in
options.description: Everyone sees the same thing and nobody signs in. Every endpoint then has to be public on purpose (SEC-007).

options.label: Not yet: on this machine and in CI
options.description: Build and test it first; choose hosting when the first deployment is due. Nothing to pay or set up now.

options.label: Azure Container Apps
options.description: Runs the app in a container that scales to zero when nobody uses it.

cost.label: Free tier
cost.free: Each month, per subscription: 180,000 vCPU-seconds, 360,000 GiB-seconds and 2 million requests
cost.price: Consumption plan, East US: $0.000024 per vCPU-second and $0.000003 per GiB-second while active, $0.40 per million requests

options.label: Azure App Service
options.description: Runs the app on a managed web server, without containers.

cost.label: Free tier
cost.free: The F1 plan: shared compute with daily limits, no custom domain certificate and no scale-out (limits not verified)
cost.price: B1, the first paid plan, East US: $0.017 an hour on Linux, $0.075 an hour on Windows

testKinds.name: Unit
testKinds.checks: One class or function: domain rules, application handlers, view models

tools.name: FluentAssertions 8
tools.note: Free only while the app isn't sold or paid for; a commercial app uses AwesomeAssertions instead (ADR-0004)

tools.name: AwesomeAssertions
tools.note: FluentAssertions' API and namespace under Apache-2.0, for commercial apps (ADR-0004)

testKinds.name: Integration
testKinds.checks: Our code plus one real outside thing: database, HTTP service, file system

testKinds.name: Functional
testKinds.checks: The whole app in memory through its real HTTP pipeline; Blazor components

testKinds.name: UI (end to end)
testKinds.checks: The running system in a real browser, accessibility included
testKinds.runs: Key paths on every PR; the full set nightly

testKinds.name: System (smoke)
testKinds.checks: The deployed app in staging actually works

testKinds.name: Architecture
testKinds.checks: Layers and modules depend only in allowed directions

tools.name: OpenAPI snapshot test
tools.note: The API's OpenAPI document must match a committed snapshot, as in the kit's sample (ContractTests.cs)

tools.name: .NET package validation
tools.note: Part of the .NET SDK; for apps that publish NuGet packages

testKinds.name: Performance
testKinds.checks: Hot paths stay within their time and memory budget

testKinds.name: Load
testKinds.checks: The deployed app keeps its response times under many users at once
testKinds.runs: On demand, before a release that changes load

tools.name: Locust
tools.note: Runs in GitHub Actions, which is free on a public repo (ADR-0057)

tools.name: Apache JMeter
tools.note: For apps that need heavy database or queue load (ADR-0057)

tools.name: Azure Load Testing

cost.label: Paid
cost.price: East US: $10 per resource per month, plus $0.15 per virtual user hour up to 10,000 and $0.06 after; each run bills at least 10 virtual users per engine for at least 10 minutes. A monthly virtual-user-hour limit on the resource stops tests at the cap

tools.note: Runs JMeter or Locust scripts at scale from Azure. The resource fee includes some virtual user hours; how many is not verified (ADR-0057)

cost.label: Paid
cost.price: Free for personal use only; any organization needs Business, $1,500 a year per company, or Enterprise, $2,500 a year

testKinds.name: Mutation
testKinds.checks: The tests themselves catch real bugs
